indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B4.5.1.1 Recognise the importance of personal hygiene
indicator.objective: Describe ways of sustaining the environment through waste management

skills.description: Identify common types of waste produced at home and school (paper, plastic, bottles, food waste, rubber).
Explain simply what separating waste means (putting different types of waste into different bins).
Describe how to separate waste into groups (e.g. plastics in one bin, paper in another).
State why separating waste is important (easier recycling, cleaner environment, less pollution).
State what happens when waste is not managed well (litter, bad smell, sickness, blocked drains).
Suggest ways to reduce waste (reuse, recycle, avoid littering).

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: All waste goes into one bin.
Burning all waste is the best way to manage it.
Littering is fine if nobody sees you.
Separating waste is only for adults.

questions.stem: Which of these is a type of waste?
hints: Which item is thrown away after use?
It is made of plastic and is often littered.
questions.explanation: A plastic bottle is a type of waste. It is thrown away after use.
questions.misconception: Only factories produce waste.

questions.stem: What does separating waste mean?
options: Putting different types of waste in different bins
hints: Think about different bins for different materials.
Plastics, paper and food waste are kept apart.
questions.explanation: Separating waste means putting different types of waste into different bins, such as plastics in one bin and paper in another.
questions.misconception: All waste goes into one bin.

questions.stem: How do you separate plastic waste from paper waste?
options: Put plastics in one bin and paper in another
Put both in the same bin
hints: Different materials go into different bins.
Plastics and paper are different.
questions.explanation: To separate plastic waste from paper waste, put plastics in one bin and paper in another. This makes recycling easier.
questions.misconception: All waste goes into one bin.

questions.stem: What can happen if waste is not managed well?
options: The environment becomes dirty and smelly
hints: Unmanaged waste piles up.
It can cause bad smells.
questions.explanation: If waste is not managed well, the environment becomes dirty and smelly. This can attract insects and cause sickness.
questions.misconception: Unmanaged waste is harmless.

questions.stem: Which of these is food waste?
hints: Which item comes from food?
It is the skin of a fruit.
questions.explanation: A banana peel is food waste. It is the leftover part of a fruit.
questions.misconception: Food waste is not a type of waste.

questions.stem: Why is it important to separate waste?
options: It makes recycling easier and keeps the environment clean
hints: Recycling needs sorted materials.
Separated waste is easier to manage.
questions.explanation: Separating waste is important because it makes recycling easier and helps keep the environment clean.
questions.misconception: Separating waste is a waste of time.

questions.stem: Which bin should you put an empty plastic bottle into?
hints: The bottle is made of plastic.
It goes into the plastics bin.
questions.explanation: An empty plastic bottle should go into the plastics bin. This helps separate it for recycling.
questions.misconception: All waste goes into one bin.

questions.stem: Which is a way to reduce waste?
hints: Reusing means using again.
It stops waste from piling up.
questions.explanation: Reusing plastic bags is a way to reduce waste. It means using them again instead of throwing them away.
questions.misconception: Burning all waste is the best way to manage it.

questions.stem: What happens when waste blocks drains?
options: Water cannot flow and may cause flooding
hints: Blocked drains stop water.
Water may overflow.
questions.explanation: When waste blocks drains, water cannot flow properly and may cause flooding. This can lead to health problems.
questions.misconception: Blocked drains are not a problem.

questions.stem: A learner puts plastic bottles in one bin and paper in another. What is this practice called?
hints: The learner is sorting waste.
Different bins for different materials.
questions.explanation: This practice is called waste separation. It means putting different types of waste into different bins.
questions.misconception: All waste goes into one bin.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a type of waste?
hints: Which item is useful and clean?
It is not thrown away.
questions.explanation: Fresh drinking water is not a type of waste. It is a useful resource. Plastic bags, banana peels and old newspapers are waste.
questions.misconception: Only factories produce waste.

questions.stem: How should food waste be separated from plastic waste?
options: Put food waste in one bin and plastics in another
Put both in the same bin
hints: Food waste and plastics are different.
They go into different bins.
questions.explanation: Food waste should be put in one bin and plastics in another. This is how we separate them.
questions.misconception: All waste goes into one bin.

questions.stem: Explain why separating waste helps the environment.
answer: it makes recycling easier and reduces pollution
separating waste keeps the environment clean and makes recycling easier
it reduces the amount of waste that pollutes the environment
hints: Think about recycling.
Separated waste is easier to recycle.
questions.explanation: Separating waste helps the environment because it makes recycling easier and reduces pollution, keeping the environment clean.
questions.misconception: Separating waste does not help the environment.

questions.stem: What is one way to sustain the environment through waste management?
options: Bury waste in the school garden
hints: Think of the three Rs.
Reduce, reuse, recycle are good practices.
questions.explanation: Reducing, reusing and recycling waste helps sustain the environment by reducing the amount of waste that pollutes it.
questions.misconception: Burning all waste is the best way to manage it.

questions.stem: What is a health risk of unmanaged waste?
options: It can attract insects and rats that spread diseases
hints: Insects and rats are attracted to waste.
They can carry germs.
questions.explanation: Unmanaged waste attracts insects and rats that can spread diseases. This is a health risk.
questions.misconception: Unmanaged waste is harmless.

questions.stem: Describe how to separate waste at home.
answer: put plastics, paper, and food waste in different bins
use separate bins for plastics, paper and food waste
separate waste into different types using different bins
hints: Use different bins for different materials.
Plastics, paper and food waste are common types.
questions.explanation: To separate waste at home, use different bins for plastics, paper and food waste. This keeps waste organised and makes recycling easier.
questions.misconception: All waste goes into one bin.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of waste separation?
options: Putting plastics in one bin and paper in another
Throwing all waste in one bin
hints: Separation means keeping different types apart.
Different bins for different materials.
questions.explanation: Putting plastics in one bin and paper in another is an example of waste separation.
questions.misconception: All waste goes into one bin.

questions.stem: Design and make a litterbin for your classroom using suitable materials. Label it clearly to show which type of waste it should hold (e.g. 'Plastics Only'). Explain how your litterbin will help separate waste.

criteria.description: Designed and made a litterbin using suitable materials
Labeled the litterbin with the type of waste it should hold
Explained how the litterbin helps separate waste

questions.answer: Teacher-assessed using the rubric. Expected outcome: a functional litterbin with a clear label and a simple explanation of how it helps separate waste.
hints: Think about what type of waste your bin will hold.
Make a clear label.
Explain how separating waste helps the environment.
questions.explanation: This is a practical task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: All waste goes into one bin.

questions.stem: Why is waste separation important for the community?
answer: it keeps the community clean and reduces diseases
separating waste reduces pollution and keeps the community healthy
it helps manage waste properly and prevents sickness
hints: Think about cleanliness.
Waste separation reduces germs and pollution.
questions.explanation: Waste separation is important for the community because it keeps the environment clean, reduces pollution and helps prevent diseases.
questions.misconception: Separating waste is only for adults.

questions.stem: Suggest two ways to reduce waste in your school.
answer: reuse paper and use reusable water bottles
avoid single-use plastics and recycle paper
use both sides of paper and compost food waste
hints: Think about what you throw away at school.
Reusing and recycling reduce waste.
questions.explanation: Two ways to reduce waste in school are reusing paper and using reusable water bottles, or avoiding single-use plastics and recycling paper.
questions.misconception: Burning all waste is the best way to manage it.
